description:
ABOUT THE ROLE

Own the data infrastructure for an AI-powered operating system serving farms. You will build the connectors and data models that bring information from disconnected farm systems into a unified platform, helping the team deliver reliable insights and agents.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Build a connector framework that makes integrating additional customers and systems fast and repeatable.

 - Develop a reliable process for AI agents to draft production-ready connectors from vendor documentation.

 - Create ways to access data without APIs, including a collector that runs on farm servers.

 - Design and maintain a canonical farm data model, including AI-proposed mappings for human review.

 - Own data quality and evaluation tools to detect when integrations or pipelines break.

 - Build tools for agents to query data and prepare machine learning training sets.

 - Investigate farm operations and occasionally connect systems on-site.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Two to four years of engineering experience building and operating production pipelines or integrations with messy data sources.

 - Strong Python and SQL skills, with experience using PostgreSQL, a data warehouse such as BigQuery, and dbt.

 - Experience designing schemas that other people and systems rely on, and resolving production issues directly.

 - Daily experience building with AI, with a practical understanding of its limitations.

 - Experience with data quality and evaluation frameworks, and an interest in real-world operating problems.

 - Experience with Airbyte, Fivetran, document extraction, or OCR is helpful.

 - Background working with ERP, IoT, agriculture, logistics, or food supply chain data is helpful.


COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

Base salary is $170,000 to $200,000 annually, plus 1% equity vesting over four years with a one-year cliff. Healthcare and work-related hardware are provided. Visa sponsorship is not available; candidates must be authorized to work in the United States without sponsorship.


LOCATION

On-site in San Francisco, five days a week, with about one week of travel per quarter to farms in Washington, Oregon, and California.
